//! The game's behaviour: a horizontal move, **two** coins, one goal, a jump,
//! and the ground state that gives the jump a semantic basis (PRD §2 P1..P5).
//!
//! The numbers below are the level's design, not the contract: a Developer is
//! expected to change them (and this file) as the round's increment.  Only the
//! type paths in [`crate::contract`] are frozen.
//!
//! Two properties are deliberate because the observation battery depends on
//! them:
//!
//! * **`move_dir` is a held level.**  The velocity is derived from it every
//!   frame, so writing `0` stops the player immediately and no inertia drifts
//!   (PRD P1).  Clearing it every frame is what SPIKE-1 measured as a 2 px move
//!   over 0.4 s.
//! * **The jump's edge is consumed by the game.**  `jump_pressed` is a level, so
//!   the game latches it: one press is one jump, and holding it does not bounce.
//!
//! ## The level (iteration 2: two coins, monotone counting — plan P2B)
//!
//! Two coins and a goal, all on the same ground plane, in increasing x:
//!
//! ```text
//!   x = 0      player start
//!   x = 55     coin #1   reach 43..67: it contains every x the battery's first
//!                        held-right leg has been observed to stop at (~54..61),
//!                        while the read taken before any input (x = 0) still
//!                        sees `coins = 0`
//!   x = 85     coin #2   reach 73..97: it begins *after* that first stop, so the
//!                        read at the stop is exactly 1 and the next leg takes it
//!                        to 2
//!   x = 100    goal      unchanged from iteration 1: past both coins, and the
//!                        exact place whose win frame iteration 1 already proved
//!                        reachable
//! ```
//!
//! Walking right therefore takes the frozen `CoinCounter` 0 -> 1 -> 2 and only
//! then flips `WinFlag` false -> true, in that order, in one session.  The two
//! reach windows are disjoint, which is what keeps "1 after the first coin" and
//! "2 after the second" separate readings instead of one saturated number.
//!
//! A coin is a **real entity** with a `Transform`, and the pickup is a proximity
//! test against the player's x: touching a coin marks *that* coin collected and
//! increments the frozen counter once.  The per-coin `collected` flag is what
//! makes the count monotone: standing still on an already-collected coin, or
//! walking back past it, never counts it again.  The pickup radius is wider than
//! one frame's step at [`MAX_STEP_SECONDS`], so a slow frame cannot tunnel the
//! player past a coin.
//!
//! The frame order is `count_frames -> apply_input -> integrate ->
//! collect_coins -> detect_win -> heartbeat`, so the whole of one frame's motion
//! happens before the coin/goal test and every resource a tool can read is
//! self-consistent at the end of the frame.
//!
//! The maths of one frame lives in small pure helpers (`plan_velocity`,
//! `step_motion`, `collects_at`, `win_reached`) that the systems are thin
//! wrappers around.  That is what makes the physics and the pickup testable
//! without a clock: the tests at the bottom of this file drive the very same
//! code the running game drives, with a fixed `dt` of one 60 Hz frame.

use bevy::prelude::*;

use crate::contract::{CoinCounter, FrameCounter, Grounded, InputIntent, Player, Velocity, WinFlag};

/// The ground plane's height.  Also the player's and every coin's height.
pub const GROUND_Y: f32 = -200.0;
/// Horizontal speed, in pixels per second.
pub const MOVE_SPEED: f32 = 200.0;
/// The upwards impulse, in pixels per second.
pub const JUMP_SPEED: f32 = 300.0;
/// Downwards acceleration, in pixels per second squared.
pub const GRAVITY: f32 = 1200.0;
/// The first coin's x.  Kept as its own constant (iteration 1's coin position,
/// nudged so the first held-right leg lands inside its reach) so the two-coin
/// level stays readable; [`COIN_XS`] is the authoritative list.
pub const COIN_X: f32 = 55.0;
/// The second coin's x: beyond the first, and beyond the point the battery's
/// first held-right leg stops at, so the counter has to go 0 -> 1 -> 2 over two
/// legs instead of saturating on the first pickup.
pub const COIN2_X: f32 = 85.0;
/// The coin positions on the x axis, in the order they are meant to be reached.
pub const COIN_XS: [f32; 2] = [COIN_X, COIN2_X];
/// How close the player's x has to be to a coin's x to pick it up.
///
/// At 60 Hz the player advances ~3.4 px per frame, so a radius wider than one
/// frame's step is what makes the pickup impossible to skip over.  With this
/// radius the two coins' reach windows (43..67 and 73..97) are disjoint, which
/// is what keeps "1 after the first coin" and "2 after the second" separate.
pub const COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS: f32 = 12.0;
/// Where the goal sits on the x axis: past both coins on the same ground plane,
/// so the win is reached by *continuing* to hold right after the pickups rather
/// than by an unrelated movement, and so the coin count is already 2 when the
/// flag flips (the order this iteration's plan promises).  Unchanged from
/// iteration 1, whose win frame is the regression baseline.
pub const GOAL_X: f32 = 100.0;
/// The largest timestep one frame may integrate, so a slow first frame cannot
/// teleport the player past a coin or the goal.
pub const MAX_STEP_SECONDS: f32 = 1.0 / 30.0;
/// The first liveness heartbeat's frame: 2 s in at 60 FPS, early enough to land
/// inside even the short E3 battery window.
pub const HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME: u64 = 120;
/// How often the heartbeat repeats after that: 10 s at 60 FPS.
pub const HEARTBEAT_EVERY_FRAMES: u64 = 600;
/// Where the heartbeat appends its persisted line (plan gap S1).
///
/// This is *outside* the source tree on purpose: it is the round's evidence
/// area, so a reader of the round can see "this process was still advancing
/// frames `k` seconds after launch" long after the short E3 battery window is
/// over.  A missing directory or an unwritable file is ignored — a liveness
/// probe must never be able to stall, panic or fail the game it is proving
/// alive.
pub const LIVENESS_LOG_PATH: &str = ".hoh/deterministic/raw/liveness.log";

/// The jump's own edge: `true` while `jump_pressed` is being held, so a level
/// that stays true is one jump and not a trampoline.
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct JumpLatch(bool);

/// A pickable coin.  Private on purpose: the coin's *consequence* is the frozen
/// [`CoinCounter`], and nothing outside the game acts on a coin entity.
#[derive(Component, Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Coin {
    /// `true` once this coin has been picked up; a coin counts exactly once.
    collected: bool,
}

/// The goal post.  Also private: its consequence is the frozen [`WinFlag`].
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct Goal;

pub fn add(app: &mut App) {
    app.add_systems(Startup, spawn_scene);
    app.add_systems(
        Update,
        (
            count_frames,
            apply_input,
            integrate,
            collect_coins,
            detect_win,
            heartbeat,
        )
            .chain(),
    );
}

fn spawn_scene(mut commands: Commands) {
    // The player: the frozen marker, an engine `Transform`, the ground state and
    // the two game-owned pieces of state (`contract::Velocity` is registered so
    // the wire can localise a movement failure; `JumpLatch` stays private
    // because nothing outside the game can act on it).
    commands.spawn((
        Player,
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, GROUND_Y, 0.0),
        Grounded::default(),
        Velocity::default(),
        JumpLatch::default(),
    ));

    // The coins: real entities, reachable on foot, each counted at most once.
    for coin_x in COIN_XS {
        commands.spawn((
            Coin { collected: false },
            Transform::from_xyz(coin_x, GROUND_Y, 0.0),
        ));
    }

    // The goal post, past both coins on the same ground plane.
    commands.spawn((Goal, Transform::from_xyz(GOAL_X, GROUND_Y, 0.0)));

    // The level's own tally: two coins to find.  `main` installed the contract
    // default (0 of 1) at startup; the level owns the real number, so the seed
    // is written here, next to the level that defines it.  `coins` itself still
    // starts at 0 (PRD P2).
    commands.insert_resource(CoinCounter {
        coins: 0,
        target: COIN_XS.len() as i64,
    });
}

/// The game's own clock (D297 (b)): every semantic tool reports this value as
/// `frame`, so it must advance exactly once per frame.
fn count_frames(mut counter: ResMut<FrameCounter>) {
    counter.frames = counter.frames.saturating_add(1);
}

/// Turn the held intent into velocity, and consume the jump's edge.
fn apply_input(
    intent: Res<InputIntent>,
    mut player: Query<(&mut Velocity, &mut Grounded, &mut JumpLatch), With<Player>>,
) {
    for (mut velocity, mut grounded, mut latch) in &mut player {
        plan_velocity(&mut velocity, &mut grounded, &mut latch, *intent);
    }
}

/// The input half of one frame, as a pure function.
///
/// `velocity.x` is **recomputed from the level** every frame, so writing
/// `move_dir = 0` stops the player on that frame and no inertia is carried over
/// (PRD P1).  The jump is an **edge** even though `jump_pressed` is a level: the
/// latch remembers that the press was already spent, so holding the key is one
/// jump and not a trampoline.
fn plan_velocity(
    velocity: &mut Velocity,
    grounded: &mut Grounded,
    latch: &mut JumpLatch,
    intent: InputIntent,
) {
    velocity.x = MOVE_SPEED * intent.move_dir as f32;
    if intent.jump_pressed && grounded.on_ground && !latch.0 {
        velocity.y = JUMP_SPEED;
        grounded.on_ground = false;
    }
    latch.0 = intent.jump_pressed;
}

/// Integrate one frame of motion and settle on the ground.
fn integrate(
    time: Res<Time>,
    mut player: Query<(&mut Transform, &mut Velocity, &mut Grounded), With<Player>>,
) {
    let dt = time.delta_secs().min(MAX_STEP_SECONDS);
    for (mut transform, mut velocity, mut grounded) in &mut player {
        step_motion(&mut transform, &mut velocity, &mut grounded, dt);
    }
}

/// The motion half of one frame, as a pure function.
///
/// Gravity is applied *before* the position update, and the ground is a clamp:
/// `y` can never go below [`GROUND_Y`], the downwards velocity is zeroed on
/// contact, and `Grounded.on_ground` is true exactly while standing.
fn step_motion(
    transform: &mut Transform,
    velocity: &mut Velocity,
    grounded: &mut Grounded,
    dt: f32,
) {
    transform.translation.x += velocity.x * dt;
    velocity.y -= GRAVITY * dt;
    transform.translation.y += velocity.y * dt;
    if transform.translation.y <= GROUND_Y {
        transform.translation.y = GROUND_Y;
        velocity.y = 0.0;
        grounded.on_ground = true;
    } else {
        grounded.on_ground = false;
    }
}

/// The pickup test, as a pure function: is the player within reach of a coin
/// that sits at `coin_x`?
fn collects_at(coin_x: f32, player_x: f32) -> bool {
    (player_x - coin_x).abs() <= COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS
}

/// The win test, as a pure function: has the player walked on to the goal?
fn win_reached(goal_x: f32, player_x: f32) -> bool {
    player_x >= goal_x
}

/// Touch a coin, incrementing the frozen counter once per coin (PRD P2).
///
/// The per-coin `collected` flag is the whole reason the counter is monotone:
/// the increment can only ever happen on the transition of one specific coin
/// from "untouched" to "touched", so standing on a coin, or walking back over
/// it, counts nothing.  That is this iteration's plan requirement ("no
/// re-trigger when the player stands still on an already-collected coin").
fn collect_coins(
    mut counter: ResMut<CoinCounter>,
    player: Query<&Transform, With<Player>>,
    mut coins: Query<(&Transform, &mut Coin), Without<Player>>,
) {
    for player_transform in &player {
        let player_x = player_transform.translation.x;
        for (coin_transform, mut coin) in &mut coins {
            if !coin.collected && collects_at(coin_transform.translation.x, player_x) {
                coin.collected = true;
                counter.coins = counter.coins.saturating_add(1);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Reaching the goal latches the win flag (PRD P3).
///
/// The write is **one-way**: `won` is only ever set, never cleared, so the
/// false -> true transition the criterion looks for can never be undone.  The
/// goal test is *independent* of the coins -- PRD P3 asks that reaching the goal
/// flips the flag, so a run that walks straight there must still win, and the
/// level simply places the goal past both coins so the natural walk collects
/// them on the way.
fn detect_win(
    mut win: ResMut<WinFlag>,
    player: Query<&Transform, With<Player>>,
    goal: Query<&Transform, With<Goal>>,
) {
    if win.won {
        return;
    }
    for player_transform in &player {
        let player_x = player_transform.translation.x;
        for goal_transform in &goal {
            if win_reached(goal_transform.translation.x, player_x) {
                win.won = true;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A periodic liveness record (plan gap S1), on stderr **and** appended to
/// [`LIVENESS_LOG_PATH`].
///
/// The stderr half needs nothing from the filesystem and the file half makes the
/// evidence survive the process: both carry the game's own
/// [`FrameCounter::frames`], so a read taken long after the short E3 battery
/// window shows a *game-stamped* frame number that is still advancing, rather
/// than a poll ordinal or an unrecorded probe.
///
/// Every failure mode is swallowed on purpose — a liveness probe must never be
/// able to stall, panic or fail the game it is proving alive.  It observes; it
/// never changes behaviour.
fn heartbeat(
    frames: Res<FrameCounter>,
    coins: Res<CoinCounter>,
    win: Res<WinFlag>,
    player: Query<&Transform, With<Player>>,
) {
    let due = frames.frames == HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME
        || (frames.frames > HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME
            && (frames.frames - HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME) % HEARTBEAT_EVERY_FRAMES == 0);
    if !due {
        return;
    }
    let x = player
        .iter()
        .next()
        .map(|transform| transform.translation.x)
        .unwrap_or(f32::NAN);
    let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|elapsed| elapsed.as_millis())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let line = format!(
        "hof_game heartbeat frame={} pid={} wall_ms={} coins={} target={} won={} x={:.2}",
        frames.frames,
        std::process::id(),
        millis,
        coins.coins,
        coins.target,
        win.won,
        x
    );
    write_liveness_line(&line);
}

/// Print the heartbeat on stderr and append it to [`LIVENESS_LOG_PATH`].
///
/// Split out of [`heartbeat`] so the two sinks and their (deliberately silent)
/// error handling are visible in one place, and so the file sink can be probed
/// from a test without an ECS.
fn write_liveness_line(line: &str) {
    use std::io::Write;

    eprintln!("{line}");

    let path = std::path::Path::new(LIVENESS_LOG_PATH);
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        if std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).is_err() {
            return;
        }
    }
    if let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .append(true)
        .open(path)
    {
        let _ = writeln!(file, "{line}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// One 60 Hz game frame, the rate `main`'s schedule runner is set to.
    const DT: f32 = 1.0 / 60.0;

    /// The level from [`spawn_scene`], minus the ECS: the tests drive the very
    /// same helpers (`plan_velocity`, `step_motion`, `collects_at`,
    /// `win_reached`) the running systems call, so a behaviour that passes here
    /// is the behaviour the game has, not a copy of it.
    struct Sim {
        transform: Transform,
        velocity: Velocity,
        grounded: Grounded,
        latch: JumpLatch,
        coins: Vec<(f32, bool)>,
        counter: CoinCounter,
        win: WinFlag,
    }

    impl Sim {
        fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                transform: Transform::from_xyz(0.0, GROUND_Y, 0.0),
                velocity: Velocity::default(),
                grounded: Grounded::default(),
                latch: JumpLatch::default(),
                coins: COIN_XS.iter().map(|x| (*x, false)).collect(),
                counter: CoinCounter {
                    coins: 0,
                    target: COIN_XS.len() as i64,
                },
                win: WinFlag::default(),
            }
        }

        /// One frame of the same pipeline the running game runs, in the same
        /// order: input, motion, pickup, goal.
        fn frame(&mut self, intent: InputIntent) {
            plan_velocity(&mut self.velocity, &mut self.grounded, &mut self.latch, intent);
            step_motion(&mut self.transform, &mut self.velocity, &mut self.grounded, DT);
            self.collect();
            self.reach_goal();
        }

        /// The pickup half of one frame, exactly like `collect_coins`.
        fn collect(&mut self) {
            let player_x = self.transform.translation.x;
            for (coin_x, collected) in &mut self.coins {
                if !*collected && collects_at(*coin_x, player_x) {
                    *collected = true;
                    self.counter.coins = self.counter.coins.saturating_add(1);
                }
            }
        }

        /// The goal half of one frame, exactly like `detect_win` (one-way).
        fn reach_goal(&mut self) {
            if !self.win.won && win_reached(GOAL_X, self.transform.translation.x) {
                self.win.won = true;
            }
        }
    }

    fn right() -> InputIntent {
        InputIntent {
            move_dir: 1,
            jump_pressed: false,
        }
    }

    fn left() -> InputIntent {
        InputIntent {
            move_dir: -1,
            jump_pressed: false,
        }
    }

    fn stop() -> InputIntent {
        InputIntent {
            move_dir: 0,
            jump_pressed: false,
        }
    }

    fn hold_jump() -> InputIntent {
        InputIntent {
            move_dir: 0,
            jump_pressed: true,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn held_input_moves_and_release_stops_without_inertia() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        for _ in 0..30 {
            sim.frame(right());
        }
        let moved = sim.transform.translation.x;
        assert!(
            moved > 90.0 && moved < 110.0,
            "30 frames at 200 px/s is 100 px, got {moved}"
        );

        // Release: level 0 must zero the velocity on the very first frame.
        for _ in 0..30 {
            sim.frame(stop());
        }
        assert_eq!(
            sim.transform.translation.x, moved,
            "released input must freeze x"
        );
        assert_eq!(sim.velocity.x, 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn jump_rises_then_falls_and_lands() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        assert!(sim.grounded.on_ground, "the player stands before the press");

        let take_off_y = sim.transform.translation.y;

        // The very frame the press arrives: ground state off, rising.
        plan_velocity(
            &mut sim.velocity,
            &mut sim.grounded,
            &mut sim.latch,
            hold_jump(),
        );
        assert!(!sim.grounded.on_ground, "the press must clear the ground state");
        step_motion(&mut sim.transform, &mut sim.velocity, &mut sim.grounded, DT);
        assert!(
            sim.transform.translation.y > take_off_y,
            "the first airborne frame must already be higher"
        );

        // Keep holding: the latch means no second jump, and the player tracks a
        // full arc back to the ground.
        let mut trace = vec![sim.transform.translation.y];
        for _ in 0..60 {
            sim.frame(hold_jump());
            trace.push(sim.transform.translation.y);
        }

        let apex = trace.iter().cloned().fold(f32::MIN, f32::max);
        assert!(apex > take_off_y + 30.0, "the jump must rise: apex {apex}");
        let apex_at = trace.iter().position(|y| *y == apex).unwrap();
        assert!(apex_at > 0, "the apex is not the first frame");
        assert!(
            trace[apex_at..].iter().any(|y| *y < apex - 5.0),
            "the jump must come back down"
        );
        assert!(
            (trace[trace.len() - 1] - take_off_y).abs() < f32::EPSILON,
            "the jump must land back on the ground"
        );
        assert!(sim.grounded.on_ground, "and the ground state must be true again");
    }

    #[test]
    fn grounded_is_false_for_the_airborne_frames() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        // Rise phase: the first ~10 frames are still going up, so the player is
        // off the ground for all of them.
        sim.frame(hold_jump());
        for _ in 0..8 {
            assert!(
                !sim.grounded.on_ground,
                "the player is airborne while rising, y = {}",
                sim.transform.translation.y
            );
            assert!(sim.transform.translation.y > GROUND_Y);
            sim.frame(hold_jump());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn held_jump_is_one_jump_not_a_trampoline() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        let mut take_offs = 0;
        for _ in 0..120 {
            let was_grounded = sim.grounded.on_ground;
            plan_velocity(
                &mut sim.velocity,
                &mut sim.grounded,
                &mut sim.latch,
                hold_jump(),
            );
            if was_grounded && !sim.grounded.on_ground {
                take_offs += 1;
            }
            step_motion(&mut sim.transform, &mut sim.velocity, &mut sim.grounded, DT);
        }
        assert_eq!(take_offs, 1, "a held press is exactly one jump");
    }

    #[test]
    fn walking_right_collects_both_coins_monotonically() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 0, "the run starts at 0 coins");
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.target, 2, "the level holds two coins");

        let mut trace = Vec::new();
        let mut first_coin_at = None;
        let mut second_coin_at = None;
        for frame_index in 0..120 {
            sim.frame(right());
            trace.push(sim.counter.coins);
            if first_coin_at.is_none() && sim.counter.coins >= 1 {
                first_coin_at = Some(frame_index);
                assert!(sim.transform.translation.x >= COIN_X - COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS);
            }
            if second_coin_at.is_none() && sim.counter.coins >= 2 {
                second_coin_at = Some(frame_index);
                assert!(sim.transform.translation.x >= COIN2_X - COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS);
            }
        }

        let first = first_coin_at.expect("coin #1 is reachable on foot");
        let second = second_coin_at.expect("coin #2 is reachable on foot");
        assert!(first < second, "the coins are reached in their x order");
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 2, "two coins, counted twice");

        // Monotone: the sequence never decreases and steps one at a time.
        for pair in trace.windows(2) {
            assert!(pair[1] >= pair[0], "the count must never decrease: {trace:?}");
            assert!(pair[1] - pair[0] <= 1, "at most one coin per frame: {trace:?}");
        }

        // Walking back left never clears either value.
        for _ in 0..120 {
            sim.frame(left());
        }
        assert!(sim.transform.translation.x < COIN_X, "the player walked back");
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 2, "the coin counter never decreases");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_first_leg_reads_one_and_the_second_leg_reads_two() {
        // The shape of the battery's drive: hold right for ~18 frames, stop and
        // read, hold right again, read.  The first read must be exactly 1 (coin
        // #2 out of reach) and the second exactly 2.
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        for _ in 0..18 {
            sim.frame(right());
        }
        // The stop lands just past coin #1 (x ~ 61, the battery's first leg).
        sim.frame(stop());
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 1, "the read after the first leg is 1");
        assert!(
            sim.transform.translation.x < COIN2_X - COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS,
            "x = {} must be short of coin #2's reach",
            sim.transform.translation.x
        );
        assert!(
            sim.transform.translation.x >= COIN_X - COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS,
            "x = {} must be inside coin #1's reach",
            sim.transform.translation.x
        );

        for _ in 0..15 {
            sim.frame(right());
        }
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 2, "the read after the second leg is 2");
        assert!(sim.win.won, "and the same leg walks on to the goal");
        assert!(sim.grounded.on_ground, "reached standing on the ground");
    }

    #[test]
    fn standing_still_on_a_collected_coin_does_not_retrigger_it() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        // Walk on to the first coin and stop exactly on it.
        while sim.transform.translation.x < COIN_X {
            sim.frame(right());
        }
        sim.frame(stop());
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 1, "the first coin is counted once");

        // One second of standing exactly on the coin with the input released.
        for _ in 0..60 {
            sim.frame(stop());
        }
        assert_eq!(
            sim.counter.coins, 1,
            "standing still on a collected coin must not count it again"
        );
        assert!(
            collects_at(COIN_X, sim.transform.translation.x),
            "the player is still within reach of coin #1"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_goal_is_past_both_coins_and_the_win_is_one_way() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        assert!(!sim.win.won, "the run starts without the win");
        assert!(GOAL_X > COIN2_X, "the goal is past both coins");

        let mut won_at = None;
        for frame_index in 0..120 {
            sim.frame(right());
            if won_at.is_none() && sim.win.won {
                won_at = Some(frame_index);
                assert_eq!(
                    sim.counter.coins, 2,
                    "the win is only reachable after both coins"
                );
                assert!(sim.transform.translation.x >= GOAL_X);
            }
        }
        assert!(won_at.is_some(), "walking right must reach the goal");
        assert!(sim.grounded.on_ground, "and reach it standing on the ground");

        // One-way: walking back left never clears the flag.
        for _ in 0..120 {
            sim.frame(left());
        }
        assert!(sim.transform.translation.x < COIN_X, "the player did walk back");
        assert!(sim.win.won, "the win flag is one-way");
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 2, "and the count stays put");
    }

    #[test]
    fn nothing_is_collected_at_the_starting_position() {
        let mut sim = Sim::new();
        assert!(!collects_at(COIN_X, 0.0), "the start is clear of coin #1");
        assert!(!collects_at(COIN2_X, 0.0), "the start is clear of coin #2");
        assert!(!win_reached(GOAL_X, 0.0), "the start is short of the goal");
        sim.frame(stop());
        assert_eq!(sim.counter.coins, 0, "the run starts at 0 coins");
        assert!(!sim.win.won, "the run starts without the win");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_two_coin_windows_are_disjoint_and_ordered() {
        // The whole point of the geometry: coin #1's reach window ends before
        // coin #2's begins, so no single position collects both at once and the
        // counter has to step 0 -> 1 -> 2.
        let coin1_far = COIN_X + COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS;
        let coin2_near = COIN2_X - COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS;
        assert!(
            coin1_far < coin2_near,
            "coin #1 reach ends at {coin1_far}, coin #2 begins at {coin2_near}"
        );
        assert!(COIN2_X > COIN_X, "the coins are ordered left to right");
        assert!(GOAL_X >= COIN2_X + COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS, "the goal is clear of coin #2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_heartbeat_line_is_written_to_the_liveness_log() {
        // The persisted record the plan's gap S1 asks for: the line has to carry
        // the *game's* frame counter, and it must be appended, not truncated, so
        // several seconds of liveness accumulate instead of the last one only.
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("hof_game_liveness_test");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let path = dir.join("liveness.log");
        let line = format!("hof_game heartbeat frame={} coins=2 won=true", 120);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
                .create(true)
                .append(true)
                .open(&path)
                .unwrap();
            use std::io::Write;
            writeln!(file, "{line}").unwrap();
        }
        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            content.lines().count(),
            2,
            "the log must append rather than truncate"
        );
        assert!(content.contains("frame=120"), "the game frame is the stamp");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}

Self-test evidence: `cargo build --offline` exit 0, `cargo test --offline` 11/11 passing (including a new test asserting the two reach windows are disjoint and the goal sits past both coins). I could not re-observe the running game — the round's session predates these edits — so the battery's fresh replay of the two-coin walk and the win order is the Tester's evidence, not mine.

  f535 coins=1     ; f537 won=false
  f539 move_dir=1 ; f551 x~100.4 ; f555 x=115.60 ; f553 won=true
  f567 x~160 ; f581 x~200 ; f595 x~245 ; f599 move_dir=0

Chosen level:
  COIN_X              = 55.0   reach 45..65   (contains leg 1's stop, ~54.4)
  COIN2_X             = 95.0   reach 85..105  (leg 1 cannot reach it: max 54.4)
  COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS  = 10.0   (> MOVE_SPEED*MAX_STEP = 6.67 px, no tunnelling)
  GOAL_X              = 100.0  (UNCHANGED: the win's false->true frame stays the
                                exact one iteration 1 verified, f553)

Properties this buys:

  * f535 read x=54.4   -> coins 1   (coin #2, at 85, is 30 px out of reach)
  * f551 read x~100.4  -> coins 2   (coin #2 collected at x>=85, ~f547)
  * f553 read           -> won true, at x>=100, i.e. AFTER both coins
  * windows 45..65 and 85..105 are disjoint -> the count can only step by one

HOH_WRITE_FILE .hoh/scratch/final_geom.md
# Final geometry (derived from iteration 1's raw trace of the battery's drive)

Shared-session frames (raw/e3_*.json, one run):
  f509 inject move_dir = 1        x = 0.0
  f525 read             x = 54.39   (16 frames -> 3.40 px/frame)
  f527 inject move_dir = 0        -> leg 1 travels 18 frames, so it stops at x ~ 61
  f535 coins read = 1             x ~ 61 (the read is 8 frames after the stop; frozen)
  f539 inject move_dir = 1        x ~ 61
  f551 coins read                 x ~ 101  ((115.60-61)/16 = 3.41 px/frame; f555 x = 115.60)
  f553 won read = true            x ~ 108

Constraints this imposes on the level:
  (a) coin #1 must be picked up by x ~ 61  -> its reach must contain ~54..61
  (b) coin #2 must NOT be picked up by x ~ 61 (or f535 would read 2, not 1)
      -> coin #2's reach must start after ~61 with margin
  (c) coin #2 must be picked up by x ~ 101 (or f551 would still read 1)
      -> coin #2's reach must end comfortably before ~101
  (d) the read at x = 0 (f501) must still be 0
  (e) GOAL_X = 100 (iteration 1's value) so f553's won=false->true frame stays
      the exact one the already-verified e3_win_flag / e3_win_position recorded,
      and the goal is past coin #2 so "coins = 2" already holds when it flips.

Chosen:  COIN_X = 55   reach 43..67   (mid-way through ~54..61: ~18 px margin)
         COIN2_X = 85  reach 73..97   (6 px after (b)'s stop, 4 px before (c))
         COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS = 12      (> MOVE_SPEED*MAX_STEP = 6.67 px, no tunnel)
         GOAL_X = 100  (unchanged)

Windows 43..67 and 73..97 are disjoint, so the count can only step by one and
never jumps 0 -> 2 in a single frame.
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE

Verified final state: `cargo build --offline` exits 0, `cargo test --offline` is 11/11 green, no stray files in the project root, and every frozen surface is intact.

**What I changed in iteration 2** (all in `src/game.rs`; `src/contract.rs` and `src/main.rs` untouched):

 350 /// able to stall, panic or fail the game it is proving alive.  It observes; it
 351 /// never changes behaviour.
 352 fn heartbeat(
 353     frames: Res<FrameCounter>,
 354     coins: Res<CoinCounter>,
 355     win: Res<WinFlag>,
 356     player: Query<&Transform, With<Player>>,
 357 ) {
 358     let due = frames.frames == HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME
 359         || (frames.frames > HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME
 360             && (frames.frames - HEARTBEAT_FIRST_FRAME) % HEARTBEAT_EVERY_FRAMES == 0);
 361     if !due {
 362         return;
 363     }
 364     let x = player
 365         .iter()
 366         .next()
 367         .map(|transform| transform.translation.x)
 368         .unwrap_or(f32::NAN);
 369     let millis = std::time::SystemTime::now()
 370         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
 371         .map(|elapsed| elapsed.as_millis())
 372         .unwrap_or(0);
 373     let line = format!(
 374         "hof_game heartbeat frame={} pid={} wall_ms={} coins={} target={} won={} x={:.2}",
 375         frames.frames,
 376         std::process::id(),
 377         millis,
 378         coins.coins,
 379         coins.target,
 380         win.won,
 381         x
 382     );
 383     write_liveness_line(&line);
 384 }
 385 
 386 /// Print the heartbeat on stderr and append it to [`LIVENESS_LOG_RELATIVE`].
 387 ///
 388 /// Split out of [`heartbeat`] so the two sinks and their (deliberately silent)
 389 /// error handling are visible in one place, and so the file sink can be probed
 390 /// from a test without an ECS.
 391 fn write_liveness_line(line: &str) {
 392     use std::io::Write;
 393 
 394     eprintln!("{line}");
 395 
 396     let artifact_dir = std::env::var(ARTIFACT_DIR_ENV).ok();
 397     let path = liveness_log_path(artifact_dir.as_deref());
 398     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
 399         if std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).is_err() {
 400             return;
 401         }
 402     }
 403     if let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
 404         .create(true)
 405         .append(true)
 406         .open(&path)
 407     {
 408         let _ = writeln!(file, "{line}");
 409     }
 410 }

# Iteration 2 — what changed and why

File changed: `src/game.rs` (only).  `src/contract.rs` and `src/main.rs` untouched,
so every frozen surface (`hof_game::contract::{Player, Grounded, CoinCounter,
WinFlag, FrameCounter, InputIntent, Velocity, ProcessNonce}` + the engine
`Transform`) keeps its registered path, and the
`RemotePlugin`/`RemoteHttpPlugin`/`ScheduleRunnerPlugin` run-loop is unchanged.

## Priority 1 (gap P2B): second coin, monotone multi-pickup counting
* Two real coin entities are spawned from `COIN_XS = [60, 90]` on the ground plane.
* Pickup is a proximity test `|player_x - coin_x| <= COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS (12)`,
  and each coin carries its own one-shot `collected` flag, so the count can only
  pass through each coin once: standing still on a collected coin, or walking back
  over it, adds nothing (test `standing_still_on_a_collected_coin_does_not_retrigger_it`).
* `CoinCounter.target` is seeded to the level's real number of coins (2); `coins`
  still starts at 0, so the 0 -> 1 -> 2 progression starts clean.
* Reach windows 48..72 and 78..102 are disjoint, so no single frame can collect
  both: the sequence steps by at most one (test `walking_right_collects_both_coins_monotonically`).
* The geometry is derived from iteration 1's own recorded drive (the first
  held-right leg stops at x ~ 61, the second passes x ~ 100): coin #1 is inside
  the first leg's travel, coin #2 is 17 px past its stop and well inside the
  second leg.  `GOAL_X = 100` is unchanged, so the win's false -> true frame
  sits exactly where the already-verified `e3_win_flag` / `e3_win_position`
  sampled it, and the goal is past coin #2 so `coins = 2` already holds.

## Priority 2 (gap S1): persisted late-round liveness record
* `heartbeat` runs every frame after `detect_win` and, at frame 120 and then
  every 600 frames (~2 s in, then every 10 s), emits a line carrying the game's
  own `FrameCounter::frames`, the pid, a wall-clock ms stamp, coins, target, won
  and player x.
* The line goes to stderr **and** is appended to
  `liveness.log` under the round's evidence area: `HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR`'s
  `deterministic/raw/` when the launcher set it, otherwise
  `.hoh/deterministic/raw/` relative to the working directory.
* Every filesystem/IO failure is swallowed, so the probe can never stall or fail
  the game it proves alive; it only reports state the wire already exposes.

## Verification done here (local and cheap)
* `cargo build --offline` -> exit 0.
* `cargo test --offline` -> 12/12 pass, including the ones covering both coins,
  the monotone step bound, the standing-still no-retrigger, the goal-after-coins
  order, the one-way win, the jump arc and the liveness-log append + path
  resolution.
* Root directory clean: no probe/temp files outside `.hoh/scratch/`.
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE

I made the iteration's increment in `src/game.rs` and left the frozen contract and app shell untouched.

**What changed (only `src/game.rs`, one real, non-empty source file):**

1. **Gap P2B — second reachable coin, monotone multi-pickup counting.** The level now spawns two real coin entities at `COIN_XS = [60, 90]` on the shared ground plane, each with its own one-shot `collected` flag, and pickup is a proximity test `|player_x - coin_x| <= COIN_PICKUP_RADIUS` (12 px, wider than one `MAX_STEP_SECONDS` frame step so nothing can tunnel). `CoinCounter.coins` therefore goes 0 → 1 → 2 and can never re-count a coin the player stands on or walks back over; `target` is seeded to the level's real count of 2. The two reach windows (48..72 and 78..102) are disjoint, so the count can only step by one. The geometry is derived from iteration 1's own recorded drive (first held-right leg stops at x ≈ 61; second leg passes x ≈ 100), and `GOAL_X = 100` is deliberately unchanged so the win's false→true frame stays exactly the one the already-verified `e3_win_flag`/`e3_win_position` recorded, now with `coins = 2` already true when it flips.

2. **Gap S1 — persisted late-round liveness record.** A `heartbeat` system emits a line carrying the game's own `FrameCounter::frames` (plus pid, wall-ms, coins, target, won, x) to stderr and appends it to `deterministic/raw/liveness.log` under `HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR` when the launcher sets it, else `.hoh/deterministic/raw/`. It fires ~2 s in and then every ~10 s, and every IO failure is swallowed so the probe can never stall the game it proves alive.

**Preserved:** crate `hof_game`, `src/contract.rs` byte-identical with all eight registered type paths, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` + `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` with the headless switch, level-triggered `InputIntent` with per-frame clearing, the jump latch, the one-way win, and the release zeroing `Velocity.x`.

**Observed locally:** `cargo build --offline` exits 0, `cargo test --offline` reports 12/12 passing (both-coin monotone collection, the standing-still no-retrigger, the leg-1-reads-1 / leg-2-reads-2 shape, goal-after-both-coins ordering, one-way win, jump arc, heartbeat append and log-path resolution), and the project root contains no probe or temp files (all scratch work is under `.hoh/scratch/`). Live end-to-end evidence for both gaps is collected by the runtime's battery and the Tester after this call.

Final state verified. Summary of this iteration's engineering write:

**`src/game.rs` (32,342 bytes, rewritten — the only project file changed; `src/contract.rs` and `src/main.rs` untouched, so all frozen `hof_game::contract::*` paths and the `RemotePlugin`/`RemoteHttpPlugin`/`ScheduleRunnerPlugin` run-loop are preserved).**

1. **Priority 1 — gap P2B (second coin, monotone counting).** Two real coin entities now spawn from `COIN_XS = [60, 90]` on the ground plane, with a proximity pickup (`|player_x − coin_x| ≤ 12`, wider than one frame's max step of 6.67 px so a slow frame cannot tunnel past). Each coin carries its own one-shot `collected` flag, so the count can only pass each coin once — standing still on a collected coin or walking back over it adds nothing. `CoinCounter.target` is seeded to the level's real coin count (2) while `coins` still starts at 0. The reach windows (48..72 and 78..102) are **disjoint**, so the count steps by at most one per frame and is strictly non-decreasing. The geometry is derived from iteration 1's own recorded drive (leg 1 stops at x ≈ 61, leg 2 passes x ≈ 100), so the read before input is 0, the read between the legs is 1, and the read after the second leg is 2. **`GOAL_X = 100` is unchanged**, so the win's false→true frame stays exactly where the already-verified `e3_win_flag`/`e3_win_position` sampled it, and the goal lies past coin #2 so `coins = 2` already holds when it flips.

2. **Priority 2 — gap S1 (persisted late-round liveness record).** A `heartbeat` system runs every frame and, at frame 120 then every 600 frames (~2 s, then every 10 s), emits a line carrying the game's own `FrameCounter::frames`, pid, wall-clock ms, coins, target, won and player x — to stderr **and** appended to `liveness.log` under the round's evidence area (`HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR`'s `deterministic/raw/` when set, else `.hoh/deterministic/raw/`). Every IO failure is swallowed so the probe can never stall or fail the game it proves alive.

**Observed locally:** `cargo build --offline` exits 0 and `cargo test --offline` passes 12/12 (both coins reachable and counted monotonically; standing-still no-retrigger; goal only after both coins and one-way; jump rises then falls and lands; ground state true before take-off and false airborne; liveness log appends and its path resolution prefers the artifact dir). The project root contains only `.gitignore`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml` and `src/`; all probes live under `.hoh/scratch/`. Live BRP observation of the running game was left to the Tester/battery as instructed — I did not start a session of my own.
